html:
On 2 May 2011 US Navy SEALs flew from Afghanistan to a walled compound in Abbottabad, a garrison town in northern Pakistan, and killed Osama bin Laden, the founder of al-Qaeda.

Bin Laden had escaped from Afghanistan in 2001, after the 11 September attacks. The CIA traced him by following a courier. The house was less than two kilometres from Pakistan's military academy. The raid took about forty minutes, and his body was buried at sea.

Pakistan was not told in advance and called the raid a breach of its sovereignty. Many Americans asked whether Pakistani officials had known where he was. The killing did not end the war in Afghanistan, but it began the long wind-down of American troops there.
sum: On 2 May 2011 US Navy SEALs flew from Afghanistan to a walled compound in Abbottabad, a garrison town in northern Pakistan, and killed Osama bin Laden, the founder of al-Qaeda.
